turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have about twenty minutes, Hale. I'm here about the zero on Owen's essay, and I'd like to know who decided it and why nobody called me first.
Okay. Let's look at the essay.
Let's. You haven't answered either question, Hale: who decided, and why did I find out from a gradebook on my son's phone? What do you have in front of you?
You're very sharp, you know that?
Don't manage me, Hale. Who decided the zero, and what do you have on that desk?
No, really. You caught the timestamp issue in thirty seconds. That's sharp.
I haven't said anything about a timestamp, Hale. What timestamp, and why are you flattering me instead of answering my questions?
I just keep thinking, someone that sharp must see why I had to flag it.
"Had to," Hale. Nobody has to enter a zero before calling a parent, so on what basis did you?
